variables.physical_definition: The free-stream flow speed far from the boundary layer (external flow velocity).
The kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity) of the fluid.
Integral from the wall to the boundary-layer edge of the square of the local mean streamwise velocity with respect to wall-normal distance (∫ U(y)^2 dy).
Boundary-layer thickness at 99% of the free-stream velocity.
Boundary-layer displacement thickness (delta*), representing the effective vertical shift of the external flow due to the boundary layer.
Boundary-layer momentum thickness (theta), a measure of momentum loss relative to the free stream.

Do not output a separate dimensional matrix or n/r/k. They are generated deterministically from this ledger. A confident name is not proof of its SI vector.

Problem statement:
Perform dimensional analysis for turbulent boundary layers under pressure gradient effects to derive the dimensionless form of the friction velocity (denoted as U_tau/U_inf). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 6 dimensional physical quantities as input parameters: 
the free-stream velocity (U_inf), the kinematic viscosity (nu), the quantity labelled MKE, obtained by integrating the square of the local mean flow speed from the wall to the boundary-layer edge with respect to wall-normal distance, the boundary layer thickness at 99% of free-stream (delta), the boundary layer displacement thickness (delta*), and the boundary layer momentum thickness (theta).
